title: Seven-cylinder radial engine with its valve train
summary: cam ring at 1/6, seven closed loops, valve gear
description: The seven-cylinder radial with its valve train: a double-track cam ring turned at one sixth of the crank speed through reduction gears, roller tappets, pushrods, rockers and poppet valves in a cut-away crankcase and opened cylinders.

difficulty.rationale: Seven articulated loops plus fourteen pushrod–rocker loops, a two-stage gear coupling, lobes drawn from a law with formula-driven followers proven by measure, multi-body fitted parts, and expert engine knowledge.

materials: Polished steel rods, crank and valve gear
Copper pushrods and spark plugs, copper-plated hub

motion.cycle: one engine cycle, two crank turns: the four strokes of every cylinder and one third of a turn of the cam ring; it closes on itself

contacts.why: the valve spring is drawn at its installed height and does not compress: while the valve is open the retainer passes into it (compression not drawn)

prompt_test.model: Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium effort, through craft3d-cli
prompt_test.result: Built and checked the engine with its valve train: 0 dof, document.check ok, every piston within 0.001 mm of the closed form at 721 samples, strokes 117.500, 117.563, 118.615 and 118.266 mm and compression ratios 5.40, 5.10, 5.03 and 5.35 (as this model's), cam ring at crank/6 reversed, tappets on the law, rollers 0.01 mm off their lobes, spigot fit 0.04 mm, least piston-to-valve 26.0 mm. It chose its own valve lash (0.25 mm, so the pad gap missed the 0.13 mm bound), compressing springs (a heavy bake) and a split cam ring, and left a piston-to-case overlap of its own unexplained; collisions were run at 25 moments only. It had to guess the valve layout, the gear train, the chamber datum, the lash, the spring and which cylinders to open; those were added to the prompt afterwards, and that wording was not retested. About 80 CLI calls.
